course_use: Reading or viewing before discovery-interview exercise; transcript works as accessible reading. Free.

title: The Evolution of StageGate: Integrating Agile and Lean for New Product Development
author_source: Robert G. Cooper, recorded short talk with transcript, Syracuse University Snyder Innovation
note: Cooper himself explains StageGate as an investment model (gates fund or kill projects) and its evolution to Agile-StageGate hybrids; short (a few minutes), transcript on page.
course_use: Primary-source clip for the NPD-process session. Free.

title: HPI D-School Basic Track (openHPI)
author_source: Hasso-Plattner-Institut School of Design Thinking, Potsdam, openHPI, self-paced since Aug 2023
note: Free design-thinking course from Germany's leading d-school: user research, insights, ideation, testable prototypes, remote team collaboration, partner project materials. Course in English; openHPI archive also has German DT courses (Strategic DT courses paid, EUR 549).
course_use: Self-study supplement for design-thinking modules; DACH source. Free (openHPI account).

title: Sawtooth Software Academy - conjoint analysis
author_source: Sawtooth Software, online academy
note: Free talk 'Uncommon Choices: Novel Applications of Conjoint Analysis in Practice' (Chris Chapman, Google; four conjoint applications for product design, managerial) and a second free talk; paid conference bundles and CBC/MaxDiff workshops. Software tutorials also at info.sawtoothsoftware.com/resources/videos.
course_use: Free Chapman talk as intro to the conjoint/concept-testing session. Free (registration) / paid bundles.

title: Bass model tutorial (Forecast Pro)
author_source: Forecast Pro (Business Forecast Systems), written software tutorial
note: Step-by-step Bass diffusion forecast: case with no history (p=0.05, q=0.41, 1 million potential market, analogous-product logic) and case with six years of data (fitted coefficients); cumulative S-curve. Software-specific but logic transfers to Excel.
course_use: Recreate both cases in Excel during the sales-forecasting lab. Free.

title: Diffusion of Innovation Theory: The Adoption Curve
author_source: YouTube explainer (channel not verified)
note: Short explainer of Rogers' adopter categories (innovators to laggards) linked to marketing by adopter segment. Third-party summary, not Rogers or Moore; check quality before use. Alternative: HRC Online 'What is the Innovation Adoption Curve?' (youtube.com/watch?v=UdaileyzAtk).
course_use: Warm-up clip for the adoption/diffusion session before Moore's chasm. Free.

title: Ethan Mollick on Embracing AI to Transform Leadership and Business Models
author_source: Ethan Mollick (Wharton Generative AI Lab), YouTube interview
note: Business-focused talk on how generative AI changes productivity, organisation and business models; length not verified. Complements his One Useful Thing posts on AI ideation.
course_use: Optional viewing for the AI-in-product-innovation session. Free.

title: IDEO Product Development (HBS 600-143)
author_source: Stefan Thomke, Ashok Nimgade; Harvard Business School Publishing, 2000, teaching case
note: Classic NPD process case: IDEO's prototyping and experimentation culture (Palm V), decision whether to accept the Handspring Visor project at half the usual development time. Good for discussing process vs. speed trade-offs and design thinking roots. Used in MIT 15.783J Product Design and Development.
course_use: Session on NPD process / design thinking; pair with IDEO ABC Nightline 'Deep Dive' video. Paid: approx. 11.95 USD per student via HBP, educator discount via HBP Education account.

title: Innovation at 3M Corporation (lead user method)
author_source: Stefan Thomke, Ashok Nimgade; Harvard Business School Publishing, 1998/99, teaching case
note: 3M Medical-Surgical division introduces Eric von Hippel's lead user method to find breakthrough ideas for infection prevention; decision which lead-user concept to pursue. The standard case for lead users and idea generation beyond focus groups.
course_use: Idea generation / open innovation session; combine with von Hippel lead user readings. Paid approx. 9-12 USD per student via HBP Education; check exact case number in HBP catalogue.

title: 3M Company (A): Building an Entrepreneurial Corporation 1902-1950
author_source: INSEAD Publishing, teaching case
note: Historical case on how 3M built an innovation culture (15 percent rule, Scotch tape, sandpaper roots). Useful counterpart to the HBS 3M lead-user case: organisation and culture rather than method.
course_use: Background or alternative to HBS 3M case for sessions on innovation culture and organisation. Paid via INSEAD Publishing / The Case Centre (approx. 5-10 EUR per copy for academic use).

title: Peloton Interactive, Inc.: Creating the Immersive Connected-Fitness Category (HBS 520-105) plus (B) and (C)
author_source: Robert J. Dolan; Harvard Business School, 2020, teaching case series
note: Category creation with hardware plus content subscription; follow-on (B)/(C) cases cover the post-Covid demand collapse and recall issues. Good for launch, pricing of a new category and over-forecasting demand. HBS Working Knowledge article on Peloton gives a free summary.
course_use: Launch and go-to-market session, or forecasting session (boom-bust demand). Paid approx. 9-12 USD per case via HBP Education.

title: Kodak and the Digital Revolution (A)
author_source: Giovanni Gavetti, Rebecca Henderson, Simona Giorgi; Harvard Business School, 2004/05, teaching case
note: Incumbent response to disruptive technology (digital imaging): cognition, capabilities and business-model inertia. Pair with Tripsas and Gavetti (2000) 'Capabilities, cognition, and inertia: evidence from digital imaging' (Strategic Management Journal), which covers Polaroid and replaces a separate Polaroid case.
course_use: Session on radical/disruptive innovation and incumbent failure. Paid via HBP Education (approx. 9-12 USD); SMJ article WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Nespresso: Strategy Reset for Growth - The Youth Market
author_source: Kamran Kashani, Goutam Challagalla; IMD, teaching case; Overall Winner, The Case Centre Awards 2025
note: Award-winning recent case: Nespresso's ageing customer base forces a rethink of product system, sustainability and brand to win Millennials and Gen Z. Good for innovation in a mature platform/system product (machines plus capsules) and Vertuo-type platform renewal.
course_use: Portfolio and platform innovation session or capstone discussion. Paid via IMD / The Case Centre (approx. 10-15 EUR per copy for academic use).

title: Red Bull (Abridged) (UV6672)
author_source: Darden School of Business, University of Virginia, 2013; distributed by Harvard Business Publishing
note: How Red Bull created the functional energy drink category with word-of-mouth, sampling and events rather than classic advertising. Austrian company; strong for category creation and launch of a radically new product concept. Full-length version UVA-M-0663 also available.
course_use: Launch / go-to-market session; Austrian example. Paid approx. 9-12 USD per student via HBP or Darden Business Publishing.

title: Red Bull Spreads Its Wiiings
author_source: Nader Tavassoli; London Business School, teaching case; Marketing category winner, The Case Centre Awards 2025
note: Brand extension and sub-brands (AlphaTauri fashion, media house) as innovation beyond the core product; follows Tavassoli's earlier Red Bull case (Overall winner, now in Case Centre Classic Collection).
course_use: Session on line extensions, brand stretch and portfolio innovation; Austrian company. Paid via The Case Centre (approx. 5-15 EUR per copy for academic use).

title: Bosch Power Tools (A) and (B): The Delta Sander Project
author_source: IMD, teaching case series
note: German NPD case: development of a new DIY power tool that broke Bosch's established development rules to achieve fast time to market; (B) case covers the problems that followed. Good for Stage-Gate vs. fast-track and cross-functional teams.
course_use: NPD process session (Stage-Gate, speed vs. quality). Paid via IMD / The Case Centre.

title: Bosch eBike Systems: entering the electric bicycle market (2009)
author_source: University of St. Gallen (HSG), teaching case, Alexandria repository
note: German-speaking case on whether and how Bosch should enter the e-bike drive market, with a business model innovation lens (component supplier vs. system brand). Bosch eBike later became market leader, so outcome can be discussed.
course_use: Business model / platform innovation session; DACH example. Access via HSG or The Case Centre; check availability.

title: Swarovski: How to Shine Through Stormy Weather?
author_source: IMD, teaching case (covers 2019-2022)
note: Austrian family company repositioning: portfolio pruning, brand reset and profitability in luxury/consumer goods. Innovation angle is brand and assortment renewal rather than technology.
course_use: Portfolio management session; Austrian example. Paid via IMD / The Case Centre.

title: The Rise of Runtastic
author_source: IMD, Research and Knowledge article (case-style narrative)
note: Austrian start-up story: from stationary tracking hardware idea (2006) to mobile app pivot after the iPhone 3G, bootstrapping, Axel Springer stake 2013, adidas acquisition 2015. Good mini-case for pivots and MVPs.
course_use: Free warm-up reading for lean startup / pivot session; Austrian start-up. Free to read online.

title: Dyson Appliances Ltd. and its Approach to Innovation (OPER087)
author_source: ICMR / IBS Case Development Centre, 2009, teaching case compiled from published sources
note: Dyson's iterative prototyping (Edison-style, one change at a time), design-led NPD and culture, covering 2000-2009. No HBS Dyson case was found; this is the cheapest dedicated Dyson case.
course_use: Prototyping / iterative design session. Low cost (ICMR cases typically a few USD); dated, update with Dyson EV cancellation 2019.

title: Tesla: Business and Operating Model Evolution (Abridged)
author_source: Stanford Graduate School of Business case collection; distributed via Harvard Business Impact and Ivey Publishing
note: Tesla's evolution from Roadster to Model 3 mass production, vertical integration and over-the-air product updates. Useful for platform strategy and the 'production hell' launch of Model 3.
course_use: Session on radical innovation scale-up and launch. Paid via HBP or Ivey (approx. 9-12 USD); search the Stanford collection by title.

title: Connect and Develop: Inside Procter & Gamble's New Model for Innovation
author_source: Larry Huston, Nabil Sakkab; Harvard Business Review, March 2006, vol. 84(3), p. 58 (practitioner article used as case)
note: Written by the P&G architects of Connect+Develop: goal of 50 percent of innovations from outside, technology scouts, networks (NineSigma, InnoCentive), examples like Pringles Prints. The standard teaching text for open innovation in FMCG.
course_use: Open innovation session reading. HBR article: WU-Lizenz prüfen (EBSCO Business Source); otherwise approx. 9 USD via HBR.

title: Innovation Simulation: Breaking News
author_source: Tucker Marion (Northeastern), Sebastian Fixson (Babson); Harvard Business Publishing, online simulation (Forio platform)
note: Single-player simulation: product manager at a struggling newspaper runs open innovation campaigns, focus groups and R&D projects under time and budget limits, then submits one idea to the CEO. Covers innovation modes and organisational context. About 60-90 minutes. A simulation titled 'Product Management Simulation' was not found in the HBP catalogue; this is the closest match.
course_use: In-class or homework simulation for idea generation / open innovation unit. Paid approx. 15-50 USD per student via HBP Education (check current price).

title: Strategic Innovation Simulation: Back Bay Battery
author_source: Harvard Business Publishing, online simulation (developed with Clayton Christensen and Willy Shih according to HBP descriptions)
note: Team or individual simulation: allocate R&D between a mature battery business and a potentially disruptive technology over several rounds. Classic for the innovator's dilemma and resource allocation. Free 3-round demo existed; full version approx. 15 USD per team license according to a 2016 Stanford course page.
course_use: Disruptive innovation session; 1-2 hours plus debrief. Paid via HBP Education (check current price).

title: Markstrat (StratX Simulations)
author_source: StratX Simulations, online marketing strategy simulation (B2C, B2B and Online versions)
note: Team-based multi-period simulation including R&D projects, product launch, repositioning and portfolio decisions in a fictitious market (Sonites/Vodites). Strong fit for NPD, positioning and portfolio management courses. University of Liège lists an individual student license at EUR 70.20 incl. VAT (2025/26).
course_use: Semester-long team simulation for Master/MBA. Paid approx. 60-80 EUR per student; instructor training recommended.

title: Cesim Global Challenge
author_source: Cesim Oy, online business strategy simulation
note: Teams manage a global mobile phone company through technology generations: R&D investment, technology-based product road maps, feature selection and launch across USA, Asia and Europe. Good for technology roadmapping and product life cycles. Cesim OnService covers service businesses (no NPD module).
course_use: Multi-round team simulation; alternative to Markstrat. Paid, per-student licence (typically approx. 40-60 EUR; request quote).

title: The Case Centre: free cases and award-winning cases
author_source: The Case Centre (Cranfield, UK), case clearing house
note: Largest case clearing house (HBP, IMD, INSEAD, Ivey, LBS, Darden etc.). Advanced search can filter for free cases and for cases with teaching notes; free educator registration gives inspection copies. Annual awards (2025 Overall: Nespresso/IMD; 2026 themes: geopolitics, sustainability, AI) are a good quality filter.
course_use: Starting point to find, preview and order cases. Free registration; cases usually approx. 5-15 GBP per copy for academic use, some free.

title: Case Centre Awards 2026: winning cases
author_source: EFMD Global blog, 23 Feb 2026
note: Overview of the 36th Case Centre Awards: winning cases on Apple, ASML, Ben & Jerry's, AI and sustainability; IMD with 50 awards in total. Useful to pick recent, high-quality cases with innovation angles (AI, sustainability).
course_use: Background for instructors when updating the case list. Free.

title: SAGE Business Cases
author_source: SAGE Publishing, digital case library (approx. 6,000+ cases from 120+ countries, incl. Sage Originals and partner cases)
note: Searchable by discipline (marketing, strategy, entrepreneurship); search 'new product development', 'innovation', 'design thinking'. Many shorter cases with discussion questions, good for Bachelor level; includes European SME cases.
course_use: Short in-class cases for Bachelor courses. Institutional licence: WU-Lizenz prüfen.

title: Emerald Emerging Markets Case Studies (EEMCS)
author_source: Emerald Publishing, peer-reviewed case journal (ISSN 2045-0621)
note: Peer-reviewed cases with teaching notes from emerging markets, including frugal and reverse innovation (useful contrast to Western NPD). Emerald also offers the Case Collection (CASE) with innovation cases.
course_use: Cases for frugal/reverse innovation sessions. WU-Lizenz prüfen (Emerald).

title: Ivey Publishing case catalogue (innovation and product management)
author_source: Ivey Business School, Western University, Canada, case publisher
note: Second-largest case publisher; search topics 'innovation', 'new product development', 'product management'. Distributes Stanford GSB cases in North America. Ivey offers selected free cases to secondary-school teachers only.
course_use: Source for additional cases. Paid approx. 5-10 USD per copy for academic use; free educator account for previews.

title: IMD case studies library
author_source: IMD Business School, Lausanne, case catalogue
note: IMD is the most awarded Case Centre school (50 awards by 2026); strong on European companies (Nespresso, Heineken, AMAG, Bosch, Swarovski, LEGO). Filter by innovation and marketing topics.
course_use: Source for European innovation cases. Paid via IMD or The Case Centre.

title: WU Case Series
author_source: WU Vienna (Wirtschaftsuniversität Wien), case studies published as numbered working papers (e.g. Donnie GmbH, Puma Prague, 2012-2013)
note: In-house WU cases; a specific WU 'EMCEE' innovation case collection could not be confirmed online. Older WU cases (incl. a Case Centre award winner on McDonald's CSR, 2014) exist. Check with WU colleagues / ePub WU for innovation-relevant cases.
course_use: Local Austrian case options; verify availability internally. Free (WU).

title: Lego Ideas: Building the Worlds You Want to See (HBS Digital Initiative student mini-case)
author_source: Harvard Business School Digital Initiative, RC TOM platform, student submission
note: Free short analysis of LEGO CUUSOO (2008) to LEGO Ideas (2014): 10,000-supporter threshold, review on play value and licensing, 1 percent royalty to creators, risk that mainly adult fans participate. No dedicated HBS LEGO Ideas case was confirmed.
course_use: Free pre-read for crowdsourcing / co-creation session; combine with ideas.lego.com live browsing. Free.

title: MIT OCW 15.783J Product Design and Development: readings and case sequence
author_source: Steven Eppinger, Karl Ulrich et al.; MIT OpenCourseWare, Spring 2006
note: Shows how a top NPD course sequences cases (IDEO, etc.) with Ulrich and Eppinger chapters, including discussion questions for the IDEO case. Useful template for building a case-based syllabus.
course_use: Instructor background for course design. Free (CC BY-NC-SA).

title: Museum of Failure (online collection)
author_source: Samuel West, Museum of Failure (touring exhibition, online catalogue)
note: Online catalogue of 150-200+ failed innovations sorted by categories (e.g. Lack to Innovate, Digital disasters, Idea Failure) with short texts; includes Google Glass, Juicero, Peloton Bike, New Coke, Amazon Fire Phone. Inclusion rule: must be an innovation and a deviation from desired results.
course_use: Group exercise: each team picks one item and diagnoses failure reasons using success-factor frameworks (Cooper). Free.

title: Google Glass Explorer Edition (2013-2015) and enterprise pivot
author_source: Google; documented in press and Museum of Failure
note: Public beta at 1,500 USD with unclear value proposition, privacy backlash ('Glassholes'), consumer stop 2015, then pivot to Enterprise Edition for logistics and manufacturing (discontinued 2023). Good for technology push vs. market pull and finding the right segment.
course_use: Discussion example for adoption (Rogers attributes, Moore's chasm). Free.

title: Juicero (2016-2017)
author_source: Bloomberg investigation, April 2017 ('Silicon Valley's 400 dollar juicer may be feeling the squeeze')
note: Over-engineered 400-700 USD connected juicer; reporters showed the juice packs could be squeezed by hand. About 120 million USD VC raised, shut down 2017. Classic example of solving a non-existent job and ignoring customer validation.
course_use: Warm-up for JTBD / lean startup sessions. Free short reading (Bloomberg may be paywalled).

title: Quibi (2020)
author_source: Quibi Holdings; widely documented (WSJ, Variety)
note: Short-form mobile streaming service raising 1.75 billion USD, launched April 2020, shut down after six months. Failure points: no social sharing, mobile-only during lockdown, no proven customer job. Contrast with TikTok.
course_use: Flop analysis exercise; compare launch plan vs. customer insight. Free.

title: New Coke (1985)
author_source: The Coca-Cola Company, company history article
note: Blind taste tests with about 200,000 consumers favoured the new formula, but the launch ignored brand attachment; Coca-Cola Classic returned after 79 days. Classic lesson on what concept and taste tests can and cannot measure.
course_use: Concept testing / market research limits session. Free.

title: Amazon Fire Phone (2014-2015)
author_source: Amazon; documented in press (Fast Company, The Verge) and Museum of Failure
note: Feature-driven (Dynamic Perspective 3D, Firefly) smartphone priced like an iPhone, exclusive to AT&T; 170 million USD write-down. Shows founder-driven feature bias and missing differentiation for customers.
course_use: Example for product success factors and positioning. Free.

title: Segway PT (2001-2020)
author_source: Segway Inc.; documented in press
note: Hyped 'it will change cities' launch, high price (approx. 5,000 USD), regulatory barriers on sidewalks; production stopped 2020. Good for over-forecasting and adoption barriers; later success of e-scooters shows timing and business model matter.
course_use: Forecasting / diffusion discussion (Bass model expectations vs. reality). Free.

title: iPhone launch (Macworld, 9 January 2007)
author_source: Apple Newsroom press release and Steve Jobs keynote
note: Integration of iPod, phone and internet communicator; multi-touch interface; launch keynote is a teaching example for value proposition framing. App Store (2008) turned the product into a platform.
course_use: Show keynote excerpt in launch session; discuss platform innovation. Free.

title: Nespresso system (capsules, machines, club, boutiques)
author_source: Nestle Nespresso SA; documented in press and IMD cases
note: Business model innovation: razor-blade model, closed capsule system with patents, Nespresso Club direct relationship, boutiques, George Clooney campaigns; later challenges from compatible capsules and Vertuo platform renewal; recycling and compostable capsules for sustainability.
course_use: Example for business model and platform innovation; link to IMD Nespresso case. Free.

title: Dyson: 5,127 prototypes and the cancelled EV
author_source: James Dyson; Dyson Ltd.; documented in press and Dyson's own communications
note: James Dyson built 5,127 prototypes over five years for the first bagless cyclone vacuum; Dyson later cancelled its electric car project in 2019 after investing approx. 500 million GBP. Shows iterative prototyping and also kill decisions at a gate.
course_use: Prototyping and Stage-Gate kill decision discussion. Free.

title: LEGO Ideas platform
author_source: The LEGO Group, crowdsourcing platform
note: Live platform: fans submit set ideas, 10,000 supporters trigger LEGO review, creators receive 1 percent royalty. Part of LEGO's turnaround story after near-bankruptcy in 2003/04 (see Robertson, Brick by Brick).
course_use: In-class browsing exercise: evaluate current submissions with screening criteria. Free.

title: Tesla Model 3 production ramp ('production hell', 2017-2018)
author_source: Tesla Inc.; documented in press and company shareholder letters
note: Over 400,000 reservations with 1,000 USD deposits (demand validation), but over-automation and bottlenecks delayed the 5,000 per week target; tent assembly line in Fremont. Good for launch readiness and scaling risks.
course_use: Launch/operations interface example; reservations as pre-test market. Free.

title: ChatGPT launch growth (100 million users in two months)
author_source: Reuters, 2 Feb 2023, citing UBS analyst note
note: ChatGPT reached an estimated 100 million monthly users about two months after launch (30 Nov 2022), the fastest consumer adoption recorded at that time. Released as a 'research preview' (low-key MVP).
course_use: Diffusion session: compare adoption curves (telephone, internet, Instagram, ChatGPT); discuss Bass p and q. Free.

title: P&G Connect+Develop open innovation portal
author_source: Procter & Gamble
note: Live portal where external inventors and firms submit technologies against P&G's published needs. Shows what an open innovation 'wants list' and submission process look like in practice.
course_use: Open innovation session: students browse needs and pitch a matching solution. Free.

title: Tchibo Ideas (crowdsourcing platform, since 2008)
author_source: Tchibo GmbH; HORIZONT report on products from customer ideas
note: German retailer's own platform linking consumers with designers to solve everyday problems; products such as a child-safe toilet brush and a cutting board with catch tray reached the shelves (2009). Format changed in 2013 to tests, surveys and workshops; current status not confirmed.
course_use: German-language example for crowdsourcing in retail. Free.

title: BMW Group Co-Creation Lab (2010 onwards) and Crowd Innovation Platform
author_source: BMW Group press release; HYVE AG (Jawecki, Bilgram, Wiegandt)
note: Virtual platform with idea contests (e.g. 'Tomorrow's Urban Mobility Services'), user toolkits, virtual concept tests and lead-user applications, aimed at long-term ties with user communities. Today BMW runs a Crowd Innovation Platform with internal and external challenges.
course_use: Example for co-creation and lead-user recruitment in automotive. Free.

title: Threadless (crowdsourced T-shirt design)
author_source: Threadless; widely documented, also HBS case 'Threadless: The Business of Community' (Lakhani, Kanji)
note: Community submits designs, community votes, company prints winners; demand risk shifted to crowd voting. Classic example of crowdsourcing plus pre-test market.
course_use: Example for user-generated innovation and voting as demand forecasting. Free (website).

title: Dropbox MVP explainer video (2007/2008)
author_source: Drew Houston, Dropbox; TechCrunch founder story
note: Before the product was finished, Houston posted a screencast demo (approx. 3-4 minutes) on Hacker News and Digg; the beta waitlist reportedly jumped from about 5,000 to 75,000 overnight. Accounts differ on details. Eric Ries uses it as the video-MVP example in The Lean Startup.
course_use: Lean startup session; show the video and ask what hypothesis it tested. Free.

title: Zappos shoe MVP (1999)
author_source: Nick Swinmurn, Zappos; told in Eric Ries, The Lean Startup (2011)
note: Founder photographed shoes in local stores and listed them online, buying them at full price only when orders came in, to test whether people would buy shoes online without building inventory or logistics. Classic 'concierge/Wizard of Oz' MVP.
course_use: Lean startup warm-up: students design an equivalent MVP for their own idea. Free.

title: Intercom on Jobs-to-be-Done (free e-book)
author_source: Intercom (Des Traynor, Paul Adams et al.), e-book
note: Practitioner book on how a SaaS company applies JTBD to product strategy, onboarding and marketing; includes the 'job story' format as an alternative to user stories. Short chapters suitable for students.
course_use: JTBD session reading or template for a job-story exercise. Free download (email registration).

title: Airbnb photography pivot (2009) as design thinking story
author_source: First Round Review, interview with Joe Gebbia
note: Airbnb revenue was flat at about 200 USD per week; founders flew to New York, met hosts and replaced amateur listing photos, roughly doubling weekly revenue and leading to the Airbnb photography programme. Illustrates 'do things that don't scale' and empathy fieldwork. The design-thinking framing is partly a later interpretation.
course_use: Design thinking warm-up; discuss which insight came from empathy vs. data. Free.

title: IBM Enterprise Design Thinking: Forrester Total Economic Impact study (2018)
author_source: Forrester Consulting, commissioned by IBM, 2018
note: Reports 301 percent ROI and 36.3 million USD NPV for a composite organisation (interviews with 4 IBM clients, survey of 60 executives); about 43 percent of benefits from faster design and development. Vendor-commissioned, so useful to teach critical reading of innovation ROI claims.
course_use: Design thinking at scale; critical evaluation exercise on evidence quality. Free.

title: SAP Design Thinking and AppHaus
author_source: SAP SE
note: Large enterprise software firm that institutionalised design thinking (Hasso Plattner, d.school/HPI) and co-innovation spaces (AppHaus) with customers. Good counterpart to IBM for B2B design thinking.
course_use: Example of design thinking in B2B / enterprise context. Free.

title: Coca-Cola Y3000 Zero Sugar: flavour co-created with AI (2023)
author_source: The Coca-Cola Company; Food Dive / Marketing Dive, Sept 2023
note: Limited edition under Coca-Cola Creations, billed as the first flavour co-created with human and artificial intelligence: consumer input on 'the future', AI-generated flavour pairings and AI mood board for packaging; QR code to AI photo filter. Taste never described. Good for discussing AI as genuine NPD tool vs. marketing gimmick.
course_use: AI in product development session; debate exercise. Free.

title: NotCo AI engine Giuseppe and The Kraft Heinz Not Company
author_source: NotCo; Kraft Heinz; Green Queen report on the joint venture
note: Chilean food-tech NotCo uses its AI 'Giuseppe' to match plant-based ingredient combinations to the flavour and texture of animal products; joint venture with Kraft Heinz (NotCheese, NotMayo) and later B2B licensing to other CPG firms. A Unilever-NotCo deal mentioned in the brief could not be confirmed; Kraft Heinz is the documented partner.
course_use: AI-driven formulation in food NPD; compare with Coca-Cola Y3000. Free.

title: Red Bull: creating the energy drink category (Austria)
author_source: Red Bull GmbH, Fuschl am See; documented in Darden and LBS cases
note: Dietrich Mateschitz adapted Thai Krating Daeng (1987 launch in Austria): new category, premium price, slim can, seeding via students and events, later media house (Red Bull Media House) and sports assets. Innovation in marketing system rather than product formula.
course_use: Austrian example for radical market innovation; link to Red Bull cases. Free.

title: Rauch Fruchtsäfte: EVIL+JUICE for Gen Z and Kloster Kitchen acquisition
author_source: Rauch Fruchtsäfte GmbH, Rankweil; about-drinks.com and Unternehmeredition reports
note: Austrian juice producer (approx. 1.8 billion EUR revenue 2025) innovates via new Gen-Z product line (EVIL+JUICE cans, launched March 2024), sugar-free variants and acquisition of organic ginger-shot pioneer Kloster Kitchen (functional drinks). Illustrates innovation through M&A vs. in-house NPD.
course_use: German-language Austrian example for portfolio innovation. Free.

title: AVL List (Graz): powertrain development and simulation-driven NPD
author_source: AVL List GmbH, Graz
note: World's largest independent powertrain engineering firm; shift from combustion engines to e-mobility, hydrogen and software-defined vehicles; strong in virtual testing and simulation that shorten development cycles. Potential guest speaker contact.
course_use: Austrian B2B example for R&D-intensive innovation and front-loading via simulation. Free.

title: Infineon Villach: 300 mm power semiconductor fab (opened 2021)
author_source: Infineon Technologies Austria AG, Villach
note: 1.6 billion EUR high-tech chip fab for power semiconductors (energy efficiency, e-mobility) and Infineon Austria's large R&D base. Example of process innovation and innovation ecosystems (Silicon Austria Labs) in Austria.
course_use: Austrian example for process innovation and regional innovation systems. Free.

title: KTM: e-mobility (Freeride E) and racing-driven product development
author_source: KTM AG / Pierer Mobility, Mattighofen
note: Austrian motorcycle maker using racing ('Ready to Race') as a development lab; early electric off-road bike Freeride E; 2024 insolvency and restructuring (Bajaj takeover 2025) show portfolio and overexpansion risks.
course_use: Austrian example; discuss brand-driven innovation and portfolio risk. Free.

title: Miro (online whiteboard) - Education plan
author_source: Miro, SaaS, current cloud version (checked Oct 2026), proprietary
note: Whiteboard with ready templates for design sprint, Jobs-to-be-Done, value proposition canvas, lean canvas and opportunity solution tree (Miroverse community templates). Free Student plan (10 team members, unlimited boards, 100 AI credits/month, 2 years) and free Educator plan (up to 100 members); institution plan from 50% off.
course_use: In-class team workshops (ideation, concept boards, sprint maps), remote group work; free for students and educators via application form

title: Mural (visual collaboration) incl. LUMA design-thinking frameworks
author_source: Mural (Tactivos Inc.), SaaS, proprietary, pricing checked Oct 2026

course_use: Practitioner guest talk on corporate innovation units and digital service innovation in an industrial firm; Vienna on site. LinkedIn for contact.

title: Johann Füller
author_source: Univ.-Prof., Chair of Innovation and Entrepreneurship, Universität Innsbruck; co-founder and long-time CEO of HYVE AG (sold to Qvest); Österreich; academic and practitioner
note: Pioneer of online communities and crowdsourcing in NPD (netnography, virtual co-creation); ran HYVE, an innovation agency, for 20+ years. Former Fellow at the NASA Tournament Lab at Harvard. Current interests: AI in innovation, open innovation, crowdsourcing, sustainability; initiated the INNCUBATOR.AT hub. Rare academic-practitioner profile with many corporate co-creation cases.
course_use: Guest lecture (remote from Innsbruck or on site) on crowdsourcing and AI in the front end of innovation, with HYVE agency cases. Master/MBA. Contact via chair page.

title: Kurt Matzler
author_source: Univ.-Prof., Strategic Management, Universität Innsbruck; academic director Executive MBA, MCI Innsbruck; Österreich; academic
note: Work on strategy, innovation and leadership incl. disruptive innovation, business model innovation, open strategy (book with Julia Hautz), customer satisfaction (Kano model research). Very highly cited; Prof of the Year 2024 (Innsbruck student council). Writes for practitioners in German, frequent speaker.
course_use: Guest lecture (remote or on site) on disruptive innovation and business model innovation for incumbents; Kano model for product feature prioritisation. Contact via chair page.

title: Matthias Fink
author_source: Univ.-Prof., Institute of Innovation Management, Johannes Kepler Universität Linz; also Grenoble Ecole de Management; Österreich; academic
note: Innovation management, strategy in innovation, socio-technical transformation and business venturing; responsible for the innovation management module in JKU's Master Leadership and Innovation in Organizations. WU Wien PhD and habilitation. Useful for the sustainability/transformation angle of innovation.
course_use: Guest lecture (remote or Linz-Vienna trip) on innovation in organisations and sustainable transformation; Master level.

title: Florian Gschwandtner
author_source: Co-founder Runtastic (sold to adidas 2015) and Tractive; co-founder Leaders21; angel investor; former judge '2 Minuten 2 Millionen'; Österreich; practitioner and communicator
note: Best-known Austrian digital product success story: Runtastic grew from app to suite of apps and own hardware (GPS watch, Orbit wearable, Moment watch), then exit to adidas. Spoke at TU Wien i2c Founder & Investor Talks ('Hurdle Race of Runtastic'). Profile sources partly older; confirm current role. German-language speaker with wide reach.
course_use: High-attraction guest talk or recorded interview on building and extending a digital product line from Austria; likely needs early booking or a fee. Good for Bachelor motivation session.

title: Marion K. Poetz
author_source: Associate Professor, Department of Strategy and Innovation, Copenhagen Business School; former Scientific Director, LBG Open Innovation in Science Center Vienna (2017-2024); Global (Austrian ties); academic
note: Austrian open innovation researcher (crowdsourcing ideas, user ideas vs. professionals, open innovation in science). Chairs the association running the Open Innovation in Science (OIS) Research Conference (Vienna 2025, Copenhagen 2026). WEF Young Global Leader.
course_use: Remote guest lecture or recorded interview on crowdsourcing problems and ideas; her classic paper on user vs. professional ideas works well as a reading. German and English.

title: Oliver Gassmann
author_source: Professor and Director, Institute of Technology Management, University of St. Gallen; formerly head of corporate research Schindler; Global (DACH); academic
note: Co-author of the St. Gallen Business Model Navigator (55 business model patterns; English Pearson edition 2025, German Hanser edition and card set) and leading DACH voice on open innovation and R&D management. Founded several spin-offs. German and English.
course_use: Remote guest talk or recorded interview on business model innovation patterns; the Navigator cards make a ready in-class ideation exercise (books: WU-Lizenz prüfen / paid).

title: Robert G. Cooper
author_source: Founder Stage-Gate system; President Product Development Institute; ISBM Distinguished Research Fellow (Penn State); McMaster University (professor emeritus status not confirmed); Global; academic and consultant
note: Originator of Stage-Gate and the most cited author on NPD success factors (Winning at New Products, 5th ed. 2017). Recent work on Agile-Stage-Gate hybrids (JPIM with Sommer) and AI in NPD. Many free white papers and webinars via software vendors.
course_use: Not a realistic guest; use his recorded webinars and the free Agile-Stage-Gate white paper as background reading for the NPD process session.

title: Eric von Hippel
author_source: Professor of Technological Innovation, MIT Sloan School of Management; Global; academic
note: Originator of the lead user method and user innovation research; books Democratizing Innovation (2005) and Free Innovation (MIT Press 2017) are both free open access (OAPEN / MIT). Essential reference for lead users and household-sector innovation.
course_use: Reading (free open access chapters) plus his recorded talks; guest appearance unlikely. Pairs with Franke/Leimüller in Vienna for a lead-user session.

title: Henry Chesbrough
author_source: Adjunct Professor and Faculty Director, Garwood Center for Corporate Innovation, UC Berkeley Haas; also Luiss Rome; Global; academic
note: Coined 'open innovation' (2003); founded the World Open Innovation Conference (2026 edition Kaunas, Nov 4-6, festschrift for his 70th birthday in Rome April 2026). Hosts the Berkeley Innovation Forum for corporate members. Many recorded talks and podcasts (Haas podcast).
course_use: Recorded talks or podcast episodes for the open innovation session; live guest unlikely.

title: Karim R. Lakhani
author_source: Dorothy and Michael Hintze Professor, Harvard Business School; Chair, Digital Data Design Institute (HBS AI Institute); co-founder Laboratory for Innovation Science (LISH); Global; academic
note: Crowdsourcing and innovation contests (NASA Tournament Lab, Topcoder field experiments) and now generative AI in innovation and teamwork (field experiments, Frontier Firm AI Initiative with Microsoft, 2025). Co-author Competing in the Age of AI. Many HBS cases on open innovation.
course_use: Recorded talks, HBS cases (paid via HBP) and his AI-teamwork field experiment as readings for the AI in product innovation session.

title: Ethan Mollick
author_source: Associate Professor, The Wharton School; author of the One Useful Thing newsletter and Co-Intelligence; Global; academic and communicator
note: Most-read academic voice on generative AI at work. Co-author (with Terwiesch, Ulrich, Girotra, Meincke, Nave) of studies on LLM-generated product ideas: LLM ideas had higher average purchase-intent quality and were far more likely to land in the top 10% (arXiv 2607.27553, revised July 2026). Free newsletter posts are good weekly prompts.
course_use: Reading and in-class replication: students generate ideas with and without AI and rate them. Guest unlikely; recorded talks plentiful.

title: Karl T. Ulrich
author_source: Professor, The Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania; Global; academic
note: Lead author of the standard NPD textbook Product Design and Development (with Eppinger and Yang, 7th ed., McGraw-Hill 2020): opportunity identification, concept generation and selection, architecture, prototyping. Co-author of the Wharton AI product idea studies with Terwiesch and Mollick.
course_use: Textbook chapters as core reading (paid; WU-Lizenz prüfen); his idea tournament method for in-class exercises.

title: Abbie Griffin
author_source: Royal L. Garff Presidential Chair in Marketing, David Eccles School of Business, University of Utah; Global; academic
note: Co-author with John Hauser of 'The Voice of the Customer' (Marketing Science 1993, among the most influential Marketing Science papers); book Serial Innovators (Stanford 2012, with Price and Vojak). Former JPIM editor; JPIM long-term impact award is named after her. Key reference for PDMA benchmarking studies on NPD practices.
course_use: Reading on VOC interviews and NPD best practice benchmarks; guest unlikely.

title: Tony Ulwick
author_source: Founder and CEO, Strategyn; Global; practitioner
note: Inventor of Outcome-Driven Innovation, the quantified Jobs-to-be-Done method (book What Customers Want 2005; Jobs to be Done: Theory to Practice 2016, free e-book on strategyn.com). Story of the failed IBM PCjr as motivation. Recorded ProductTank San Francisco talk and Ask-Me-Anything webinars. Note: Strategyn success-rate claims are vendor marketing.
course_use: Recorded ProductTank talk as warm-up; JTBD opportunity scoring as hands-on lab. Remote Q&A possibly feasible.

title: Steve Blank
author_source: Adjunct Professor, Management Science & Engineering, Stanford University; serial entrepreneur; Global; academic and communicator
note: Creator of Customer Development (The Four Steps to the Epiphany; The Startup Owner's Manual) and the Lean LaunchPad class, adopted by NSF I-Corps. Blog steveblank.com has free teaching materials, syllabi and recorded lectures.
course_use: Free blog posts and Lean LaunchPad materials for the lean startup session; customer discovery interviews as student assignment.

title: Alexander Osterwalder
author_source: Co-founder, Strategyzer; Global (Swiss); practitioner and communicator
note: Co-inventor of the Business Model Canvas and Value Proposition Canvas; co-author of Value Proposition Design and Testing Business Ideas (with David Bland, 2019, 44 experiment cards). Thinkers50 regular. Free canvases and many free videos.
course_use: Value Proposition Canvas and assumption mapping as workshop tools; recorded talks. Live booking is via speaker bureaus (expensive).

title: Rita Gunther McGrath
author_source: Professor, Columbia Business School; Global; academic and communicator
note: Discovery-driven planning (assumption-based planning that anticipated lean startup), The End of Competitive Advantage (2013), Seeing Around Corners (2019) on inflection points. Thinkers50 top 10, strong newsletter and podcast presence.
course_use: Discovery-driven planning reverse income statement as exercise for project teams; recorded talks.

title: Teresa Torres
author_source: Product discovery coach; founder Product Talk; author Continuous Discovery Habits (2021); Global; communicator/practitioner
note: Opportunity Solution Tree (outcome, opportunities, solutions, assumption tests) and weekly customer interviewing; the de facto standard for continuous product discovery in software product teams. Blog posts free, courses paid.
course_use: Opportunity Solution Tree as in-class tool for digital product innovation; blog posts as readings.

title: Marty Cagan
author_source: Founder and Partner, Silicon Valley Product Group (SVPG); Global; practitioner and communicator
note: Books Inspired (2nd ed. 2017), Empowered and Transformed (2024, product operating model). Defines the empowered product team, product discovery vs. delivery. Free SVPG articles; speaker at #mtpcon London 2026.
course_use: Readings on how tech firms organise product innovation (contrast with Stage-Gate); free SVPG articles.

title: Lenny Rachitsky
author_source: Author Lenny's Newsletter and host Lenny's Podcast; ex-Airbnb product lead; Global; communicator
note: Largest product management newsletter on Substack (about 1.2M subscribers per First Round Review) and top tech podcast; long-form interviews with product leaders on discovery, launch, growth and AI products. Many posts paywalled; podcast free.
course_use: Assign podcast episodes as case-like listening (e.g., how a specific product was launched); free.

title: Petra Wille
author_source: Independent product leadership coach; author STRONG Product People (2021); Global (DACH, Germany); communicator/practitioner
note: German-speaking product leadership coach; book on developing product managers, #52questions coaching cards. Well known speaker in the Mind the Product community. Location and current speaking record not verified.
course_use: Remote guest talk (German or English) on the product manager role and competencies; useful career-oriented session for students.

title: PDMA DACH Community (Product Development and Management Association)
author_source: PDMA, regional community for Germany, Austria, Switzerland; professional association
note: PDMA (founded 1976) publishes the Journal of Product Innovation Management and runs the NPDP certification and the PDMA Body of Knowledge; the DACH community connects product innovators, product managers and developers plus consultants and research institutes with regular networking events. Source for practitioner speakers in the region.
course_use: Speaker pool and events; point students to NPDP as career credential and to JPIM (WU-Lizenz prüfen). Membership paid.

title: ISPIM Innovation Conference
author_source: International Society for Professional Innovation Management (ISPIM); annual conference
note: Largest academic-practitioner innovation management conference in Europe; 2026 edition Granada, 7-10 June ('Connecting for Innovation'), plus regional events (Bangkok March 2026). 2027 location not yet confirmed. Proceedings and session recordings give current practitioner cases.
course_use: Background for instructor; PhD/Master students can attend; source of guest speakers. Paid registration.

title: IPDMC - Innovation and Product Development Management Conference
author_source: Academic conference series (formerly administered by EIASM); 2026 hosted by KTH Stockholm
note: Core European research conference on NPD and innovation management (33rd edition June 2026, theme 'Innovation in times of unrest', 446 registrations, run fully digital). Caveat: EIASM filed for bankruptcy on 1 April 2026; organisation of future editions is being rebuilt, check before planning.
course_use: Research community for Master thesis topics and instructor networking; not a student event.

title: R&D Management Conference (RADMA)
author_source: R&D Management Association (RADMA) and R&D Management journal; annual conference
note: 2026 edition Manchester, 22-24 June ('Creativity and resilience in an era of technological disruption'), tracks on business model innovation, ecosystems, open innovation with AI and platforms, IP. Strong academic-industry mix.
course_use: Instructor networking and source of recent research; doctoral colloquium for PhD students. Paid.

title: World Open Innovation Conference (WOIC)
author_source: Founded by Henry Chesbrough (2014); now chaired by Marcel Bogers (TU Eindhoven, ITEM)
note: Open innovation research plus best-practice track for corporate and public-policy contributions; WOIC 2026 in Kaunas, Lithuania, 4-6 November. WOIC Insights newsletter on Substack.
course_use: Background and recordings for the open innovation session; corporate best-practice track as case source.

title: Open Innovation in Science (OIS) Research Conference
author_source: Association for Advancing Science and Innovation; originally LBG Open Innovation in Science Center, Vienna
note: Vienna hosted the 6th edition in May 2025 (keynote Scott Stern); 7th edition at CBS Copenhagen, 11-13 May 2026, with free online plenary sessions. Vienna roots make it a link into the local open innovation research community (LBG).
course_use: Free online plenaries as optional viewing; network for Vienna-based open innovation speakers.

title: Mind the Product (#mtpcon) and ProductTank meetups
author_source: Mind the Product (owned by Pendo); global product management community, conferences and volunteer-run local ProductTank meetups
note: Largest product management community; #mtpcon London (June 2026, 1,000+ attendees, speakers from SVPG, Slack, FT, Booking.com) with recap pages and free talk videos. ProductTank meetups are free. A ProductTank Vienna appears active per LinkedIn recaps, but no official chapter page was found (mindtheproduct.com/producttank/vienna returns 404); check Meetup/LinkedIn.
course_use: Free talk videos as tutorials on discovery, roadmaps, launch; send students to a local ProductTank evening; source of practitioner guest speakers.

title: Product Management Festival (Zurich)
author_source: Independent, community-run product management conference, Zurich (since 2019)
note: Closest major German-speaking product conference; community-voted talks, no sponsor keynotes; 2026 edition 27 November 2026 in Zurich (about 45 speakers). Talk recordings from past years online.
course_use: Recorded talks as tutorials; speaker list as DACH guest speaker pool. Paid tickets.

title: ViennaUP
author_source: Vienna Business Agency (Wirtschaftsagentur Wien); decentralised start-up and innovation festival
note: City-wide festival, 2026 edition 18-22 May with 50+ events at 29 locations; topics AI, sustainability, manufacturing, scaling, corporate-start-up matchmaking (Connect Day). Many events free.
course_use: Field trip / assignment: students attend an event and report on a launch or innovation pitch; speaker scouting.

title: AustrianStartups
author_source: Non-profit association, Austrian start-up community (podcast, newsletter, events in all federal states, AustrianStartups Summit)
note: Largest Austrian founder community; annual Summit in Vienna (keynotes, masterclasses, pitches), founder peer circles, tech podcast and newsletter, free community platform listing start-ups and events. Good access to Austrian founders for lean startup / product-market-fit stories.
course_use: Source of start-up guest speakers and student project partners; podcast episodes as listening.

title: Co-Creation Lab Vienna (Wirtschaftsagentur Wien)
author_source: Vienna Business Agency; public co-creation and innovation workshop programme
note: City programme where Viennese companies bring an innovation project (e.g. product development) to workshops with experts from firms, research and administration. Shows applied co-creation in local SMEs; programme description PDF, check whether still running.
course_use: Example of public innovation support; possible project-partner or guest from the Vienna Business Agency innovation team.

title: Plattform für Innovationsmanagement (PFI)
author_source: Austrian network of innovation managers from industry and research (founded 2003); annual Forum Innovation
note: Austrian practitioner network for corporate innovation managers; annual Forum Innovation (e.g. 12th edition 2015, Perchtoldsdorf). Sources found are old; current activity level not confirmed.
course_use: If active, a route to Austrian industry innovation managers as guest speakers; verify first.
